question: How do I start a new student organization at IIT?
gold_answer: Complete registration form, create a proposal, create an example budget, get SGA review and approval
answer:
Here are the steps to start a new student organization at IIT:

1.  Complete the Group Registration form on 312. This allows the Office of Student Life to review the preliminary outline of your proposed student organization before scheduling an initial meeting. This initial meeting is an opportunity for interested organizations to share the purpose and goals and receive an overview of the Student Government Association (SGA) process for approving new student organizations.
2.  Work with the Office of Student Life to finalize your proposal. The proposal should be approximately 2-3 pages in length and must include:
    *   Organization name
    *   Purpose and Goals
    *   Constitution and/or Bylaws (you can find a sample constitution here)
    *   How the organization will benefit students
    *   How the organization is different from currently existing organizations
    *   How the organization plans to recruit members
    *   Current executive board members/structure
    *   List of programs and events
    *   At least seven interested students, including name, email address, major, and class year
    *   Potential advisor(s)
    *   Sample budget using the SGA preferred format (this budget must include a breakdown of budget categories, and it is capped at a total of $4,000 per semester for the first two semesters).
3.  Create an example budget while working on your proposal. SGA reviews budgets carefully before confirming an organization, so be as specific as possible.
4.  Create a sample constitution. To receive your organization funding, your constitution must be shared with the AD and approved by them.
5.  Once all documents have been approved, students must submit all relevant documents via the New Student Organization Request Form before the end of Week 8 of the semester.
6.  As SGA reviews your documents, you may be asked to present at an SGA meeting. If required, create a presentation based on your proposal. This presentation should be five minutes or less, followed by five minutes to answer questions.

You can contact any member of the Office of Student Life with any questions regarding the new student organization process.

question: How do I get reimbursed for something I bought for my club?
gold_answer: Submit an Expense Claim on Buy It within 10 days of the purchase with receipts
answer:
To get reimbursed for something you bought for your club, here are the steps and conditions:

*   **General Reimbursement:**
    *   Members of student organizations can purchase items using their own personal funds and be reimbursed, only if it was approved for their budget in BuyIt.
    *   If any student makes a purchase using their personal funds on behalf of a student organization, they should submit an Expense Claim on Buy It within 10 days of the purchase.
    *   In order to be reimbursed, students must ensure that they provide receipts for all purchases they are seeking reimbursement for.
    *   Reimbursement can take approximately sixty (60) days from the time of submission.
    *   In most cases, the reimbursement will come in the form of a check mailed to the student at the mailing address they provide in the reimbursement submission. For those that have direct deposit, you are still required to share an updated address on your reimbursement form.
    *   Reimbursements cannot exceed $500 per student, per event– no exceptions.
    *   Reimbursements for catering cannot exceed $300.

*   **Expense Claim Details (for approved items):**
    *   An expense claim (or reimbursement) is an out-of-pocket expense for an approved item from your budget (which was allocated by the Finance Board) that you are requesting a refund for.
    *   The Treasurer of the organization is the only person who can submit expense claims. The President may submit on occasion to assist the Treasurer.
    *   Anything approved on the budget approval that cannot be found on Buy It may be purchased externally and reimbursed.
    *   When submitting a receipt on behalf of another student within the organization, you must ensure their name appears in the “On Behalf Of” drop down feature. If the student is not included in the dropdown box, please email Sarah Hessasta will the full name, Hawk email and A# of the student you wish to include in the dropdown feature. Once the student is successfully inputted into the dropdown feature, you may proceed with the expense claim submission.
    *   The student must take a screenshot or photo of their receipt and ensure that it is shared with their treasurer as soon as possible.
    *   All receipts must include the name of the vendor, the date the items were purchased, a list of the items themselves and proof of payment, meaning it must show that the item was paid in cash or with a card. If it was paid with a card, the last four digits of the card would need to be on the receipt.
    *   In the description box, you must write a brief (one sentence max) justification of the items purchased, along with the address of the person being reimbursed and whether.

*   **Reimbursement Deadlines:**
    *   For purchases made in the Fall semester (August-December), students must submit their reimbursement no later than December 20th.
    *   For purchases made in the Spring semester (January-May), students must submit their reimbursement before May 1st.
    *   Reimbursements submitted late will automatically be denied and the student will not be reimbursed.

*   **Reimbursement by Treasurer for Member:**
    *   Reimbursements may be submitted by the Treasurer for an expense incurred by another student organization member. The member must be a current student of Illinois Tech or VanderCook, and may not be an external advisor.

*   **Ticket Discount Reimbursement:**
    *   If a student organization is receiving a discount by purchasing multiple tickets at one time, the following must be followed to receive a reimbursement:
        *   Students must contact the OSL office to set up an online ticket store.
        *   Students will pay their share to the online ticket store.
        *   One student may pay for all of the tickets and submit a reimbursement for the amount that was covered by the SAF.
    *   IMPORTANT: Students should not be collecting money from other students and then reimbursing them at a later time. These requests will automatically be denied, and no student will be reimbursed.

question: How do we set up fundraising for my club on 312?
gold_answer: Email the Student Life Coordinator Sarah Hessasta a minimum of one week prior
answer:
The way you set up fundraising depends on whether it is small-scale or large-scale.

For **Small Scale Fundraising** (like selling items or organizing a car wash):
*   You must email the Student Life Coordinator, Sarah Hessasta (shessasta@iit.edu), a minimum of one week prior to when you need the ticket store available.
*   Your email must include the following:
    *   Name of fundraiser
    *   Cost of the item(s) to purchase
    *   How many of each item is for sale
    *   Date the store needs to be open
    *   Date the store should close
    *   Email address of treasure to be notified of purchases and keep track of funds
    *   Image to include on the store for students to see (must be jpeg or png format - 800x800 pixels)
*   The Office of Student Life can create an online ticket store on the 312 to collect money electronically.
*   If you are collecting cash or checks, checks must be made out to “Illinois Institute of Technology” to be deposited.
*   All cash and checks collected should be placed in an envelope labeled with the name of the organization, their 6-digit Fund Number, and the total balance of cash and checks that are enclosed.
*   The envelope should be delivered to the Student Life Coordinator Sarah Hessasta to be deposited into.

For **Large Scale Fundraising** (like asking for alumni/company donations/sponsorship):
*   All large-scale fundraising must go through the Office of Advancement to ensure policy/procedure is followed for these requests for a non-profit university.
*   Any fundraising from individuals outside of the university requires approval from Institutional Advancement.
*   To begin this process, you must contact Joe Volin (jvolin@iit.edu) a minimum of 90 days prior to the intended fundraising date.
*   In your initial email, you should have created a proposal that includes the following:
    *   Mission of the student organization
    *   What they need funding for:
        *   Project / Event / Etc. Explain what it is, who is involved, how it benefits students (learning outcomes)
    *   What they are looking for help with:
        *   Money (total amount needed), Prizes (like t-shirts, water bottles, etc.), etc, sponsorship of event
    *   Benefits for alumni/companies to donate (advertise their company in marketing materials, space to table at the event to meet with IIT students, etc.)
*   Students can reach out to the Student Life staff for initial assistance in creating their proposal.
*   If your fundraising proposal is part of an event, the event form on 312 will prompt you for the additional information required to evaluated your request from Advancement.

If Finance Board requires you to ticket your event, all tickets must be sold and managed through 312.

question: How much does it cost to reserve the MTCC ballroom?
answer:
For the MTCC/Hermann Hall/Bog Space, the space itself is free, but it can become costly due to equipment or staffing needs.

When submitting your budget to the Finance Board, you should take into account common charges, as university policy requires fees to be added to large-scale and/or after-hours events. OSL cannot remove or discount the costs of staffing, work orders, and/or equipment set by the university.

Here are some estimated costs for common charges:
*   **Staffing: Public Safety:** $50 per hour, with a minimum of 4 hours. This is required if 50 guests or more and/or if open to outside guests are attending (regardless of size).
    *   50-100 attendees = 1 officer
    *   100-150 = 2 officers
    *   150-200 = 3 officers
*   **Staffing: Janitorial:** $40 per hour, with a minimum of 4 hours. This is required if there are 50 guests or more, and anytime food is being served at an event outside of the university's janitorial hours.
*   **Staffing: AV Tech:** $22 per hour. This is required for any event in MTCC or Hermann Hall using audio/visual systems.
*   **Staffing: Extended Staffing:** $20 per hour. This is required if in MTCC or Hermann Hall for each hour outside of the event hours.
    *   The example given is: Saturday event in Hermann Hall starting at 5PM-8PM -> charged from 3PM-8PM.
    *   This is required if in MTCC or Hermann Hall for each hour outside of the event hours, which is defined as:
        *   ∉ Monday-Friday 8am-8pm
        *   ∉ Sat-Sunday 9am-3pm
*   **Equipment:**
    *   Chairs, tables, coatrack: No Charge if inside; Rental charge (varies) for outside events. Outside equipment requires at minimum 2 week notice.
    *   Power strip: $12.00 per power strip (minus 75% discount) = $3.00.
    *   Wireless Microphone: $90.00 per microphone (minus 75% discount) = $22.50.
    *   Linens: $7.00 per linen (minus 75% discount) = $1.75 per linen.

Please note that failure to acknowledge these mandated fees in the budget submission will result in a deduction from approved budget costs or a reimbursement from the student organization during the following semester. Also, this list of charges is not the full list of potential charges and was last updated in January 2024, and prices are subject to change; final estimates are reflected on your space reservation confirmation sheet.

If you are planning a large event, remember that large events are defined as any events that are:
*   More than 50 guests
*   Open to the public (non-IIT/Vandercook students, staff, and faculty)
*   Has extensive AV / equipment needs
*   Considered a gala / banquet / performance
*   Requires multiple rooms to be reserved
*   Requests large spaces on campus (HH/MTCC Auditorium, Ballroom)

Large events are produced in partnership with Event Services, and typically require a minimum of four weeks lead time to ensure all details are confirmed.

question: what documents do I need to submit to get my new org approved
gold_answer: Complete the Group Registration form on 312, create a proposal, draft a constitution, get reviewed by the Assistant Director, then submit to SGA Senate for approval
answer:
To get your new organization approved, you need to complete several steps and create specific documents:

*   Create a sample constitution. To receive your org funding, your constitution needs to be shared with the AD and approved by them.

question: my club bought some reusable equipment with SAF money, where do we store it
gold_answer: Items purchased with SAF funding must be stored in the MTCC basement or in dedicated student organization space
answer:
Student organizations that purchase reusable items with SAF funding must keep those items in the storage areas located in the MTCC basement or in dedicated student organization space.

If you are storing items in the MTCC basement area, you need to adhere to these guidelines:

*   An organization's items must be stored in a container clearly labeled with the organization’s full name (and acronym if it applies) and email address.
    *   The only exception will be if the item itself is too large to fit into a container. Oversize items will still need to be clearly labeled with the organization’s full name and email address.
    *   If you need a clear plastic bin to store your items, please request it in your next Finance Budget.
*   All items belonging to an organization must be organized and situated together in the same vicinity.
*   All contents must be clean, organized and accessible (Ex. Loose colored pencils are tied together with a rubber band. Loose papers are clipped together with a paperclip. A decorative garland is tightly wrapped and protected for future use).
*   The storage area can only be accessed during the hours the Commons dining hall is open, with an escort of either an OSL staff member or a Welcome Desk employee.
*   The President is responsible for maintaining an inventory of the items stored in the unit and will be responsible for submitting the inventory at the end of each academic semester.
*   The storage area must be kept clean and organized.
*   Student Organization Storage Space, and any organization offices/spaces, are not to be used for personal item storage. Any personal items that do not belong to the university may be removed.
*   Items unaccounted for or improperly labeled at the end of the academic semester, will belong to the Office of Student Life and/or be discarded.
*   Presidents and Treasurers can request access to the basement by filling out the Space Access Request form.

The following items are prohibited from being stored in the MTCC storage unit – no exceptions:

*   Food and beverages – both opened and sealed
*   Personal items of any organization member or otherwise
*   Used napkins, utensils and other kitchen items
*   Items broken beyond repair
*   Lighters and other highly flammable materials
*   Items already prohibited by the university

Failure to adhere to these rules will result in a loss of access to the MTCC storage unit and could lead to additional consequences for the organization itself.

question: my club wants to travel to a conference out of state, what do we need to do
gold_answer: Get Finance Board approval, attach conference registration and travel documents to your ledger, book travel through Buy It and Concur, and arrange for a faculty or staff member to accompany the group
answer:
Here are the steps your student organization needs to take for traveling to a local or out-of-state conference or competition:

*   **Several months out:**
    *   The organization will seek out their advisor or another willing staff or faculty member to accompany the student organization on their trip.
    *   The Treasurer will submit a budget. The Finance Board will fund a conference/competition in full, covering registration, transportation, and lodging, though the number of travelers allowed to travel will fluctuate. The conference/competition will be ticketed.
    *   Advisors can connect with the Student Life Coordinator to book their individual travel.
*   **Supporting Documents:** Supporting documents and links to the conference registration, preferred travel and lodging items, etc., must be attached to your ledger for consideration by the Finance Board.
*   **75-60 days out:** All students must submit a Dean of Students (DoS) Travel Form upon budget approval. Treasurers must wait for DoS approval before any bookings can be made or approved. Remember, there is a fee for Concur submissions that are canceled.
*   **After DoS Approval:** Student leaders will be invited into a formal Student Travel Checklist that starts with a meeting with Sarah Hessasta.
*   **45 days out:** Student leaders will schedule a meeting with Sarah Hessasta to establish a formal registration for the approved conference/competition. Students will be guided through the Travel Checklist that includes Concur registration, travel booking, and ticketing.
*   **Ticket Purchase:** The conference will now be ticketed. Tickets must be purchased before travel but before the allotted deadline. Debts not paid will result in the student not traveling.

Additionally, please note these details regarding travel and funding:

*   A chaperone is required for all student travel, and this must be a full-time Illinois Tech staff or faculty member. The Office of Student Life will handle the chaperone’s registration, lodging, and transportation.
*   The SAF will cover registration, lodging, and transportation in full, but travelers will be required to pay a ticket for their attendance before traveling. question: how do i do the buy it thingy for reimbursment
gold_answer: To get reimbursed, submit an expense claim through Buy It. The purchase must have been in your approved budget. Upload your receipts and the payment will be processed.
answer:
Here are the steps for submitting an expense claim (reimbursement):

*   An expense claim is for an out-of-pocket expense for an approved item from your budget (which was allocated by the Finance Board) that you are requesting a refund for.
*   The Treasurer of the organization is the only person who can submit expense claims, though the President may submit on occasion to assist the Treasurer.
*   You must take a screenshot or photo of your receipt and ensure that it is shared with your treasurer as soon as possible.
*   All receipts must include:
    *   The name of the vendor.
    *   The date the items were purchased.
    *   A list of the items themselves.
    *   Proof of payment, meaning it must show that the item was paid in cash or with a card. If it was paid with a card, the last four digits of the card would need to be on the receipt.
*   In the description box, you must write a brief (one sentence max) justification of the items purchased, along with the address of the person being reimbursed.
*   Expense claims must be submitted within 10 days of the purchase, or the expense claim may not be approved.

If you are submitting a receipt on behalf of another student within the organization, you must ensure their name appears in the “On Behalf Of” drop down feature. If the student is not included in the dropdown box, you must email Sarah Hessasta with the full name, Hawk email, and A# of the student you wish to include in the dropdown feature. Once the student is successfully inputted into the dropdown feature, you may proceed with the expense claim submission.

For more detailed information, you can use the following helpful links:
*   Login to Buy It
*   Buy It Training Video
*   How to submit a reimbursement

Please note that reimbursements can only be for current Illinois Tech (or Vandercook) students, faculty, and staff; Student Life cannot approve reimbursements for alumni, former students, or external entities for student organization expenses.

question: WHAT IS BUY IT AND HOW DOES IT WORK
gold_answer: Buy It is IIT's procurement system for student organizations. It is used to request purchases and process reimbursements. All expenses must go through Buy It using your org's approved budget.
answer:
Illinois Tech uses an online purchasing system called Buy It.

Here is how it works:

*   **Access:** Organization treasurers and presidents are granted access to Buy It after completing required training provided by the Office of Student Life.
*   **Usage:**
    *   Treasurers can make approved purchases on behalf of their organization or submit an expense claim (also known as a “reimbursement”).
    *   Presidents will also be granted Buy It access to assist Treasurers, if needed.
*   **Purchasing Rules:**
    *   Purchases in Buy It should only be made following approval of a budget and its items from the Finance Board, and never for personal goods.
    *   BuyIt is used in partnership with 312 to ensure that all purchases are accounted for.
    *   After submitting a request in BuyIt, ensure to submit the payment request from the budget line that is funding the request!
    *   All purchases should be re-assigned to Sarah Hessasta.
*   **Requisitions:**
    *   Requisitions are what carts in Buy It once approved by Student Life Coordinator, Sarah Hessasta.
    *   Requisitions are used to generate payment through Buy It to approved vendors and select punch-out catalogs.
    *   Treasurers have access to create carts (which become requisitions) through Buy It.
*   **Purchase Orders (POs/PEs):**
    *   "PO" stands for “Purchase Order,” (at Illinois Tech we call POs “PEs”) which is a requisition that has been fully approved and is ready for payment.
    *   If your vendor has questions about the Illinois Tech PO process, they can contact the Procurement Office directly through the information listed on their website.
*   **External Purchases:** When purchasing items outside of Buy It, students must present the sales tax exemption form because Illinois Tech is a non-profit university and all purchases made for Illinois Tech are sales tax exempt. Students will not be reimbursed for sales tax.
*   **Approval:** BuyIt transactions are linked to your specific student organization account, often called a “FOAP” – which stands for “fund, organization, account, program.” Student organization purchases follow the same approval queues as faculty/staff purchases, and depending on the vendor, dollar amounts, or contractual nature of a requisition, there is a minimum of levels of approval for all purchases, and often times, more than three.

question: approval process
answer:
The process for a new student organization to be approved involves several steps:

*   During the first eight weeks of each semester, students can work with the Office of Student Life to finalize the documents required to create a new student club/organization.
*   For the student club/org to be approved, an official proposal must be created, along with a constitution and sample budget. These documents will then be reviewed and approved/denied by the Student Government Association (SGA) during the second half of the semester.
*   Once all documents have been drafted, reviewed, and approved by the Assistant Director of Student Life, students must submit all relevant materials via the Potential New Student Organization review form by the Friday of the 8th week of the semester.
*   The submitted documents will be reviewed by the SGA Executive Vice President.
*   SGA will then spend the next two weeks reviewing proposals and contacting potential new student organizations with questions.
*   If, after the completion of the review period, SGA is satisfied with all proposal materials, it will approve the student organization at week 10 of the semester.
*   If SGA cannot decide by vote to approve an organization, it will invite student representatives of said organization to present on behalf of the organization at a Senate meeting. A subsequent vote will take place in which an organization is either approved or denied outright.
*   If approved, the SGA Executive Vice President will email each approved organization, notifying them of their status.
*   A complete list of approved organizations and their budgets will be sent to the Finance Board before week 11 and no later than week 12.
*   The Finance Board will hold a hearing within a week of receiving a complete list of approved organizations to review the submitted budget requests from the newly approved organizations and the Finance Board will evaluate budget proposals based on:
    *   The organization's stated goals and activities
    *   Alignment with existing campus funding policies and the organization’s expected financial needs
    *   Compliance with university regulations and finance board policies
    *   Any additional financial context provided by the approved organizations if requested by the Finance Board.
